4) Evidence appendix: sanitized config snippets (security group, route table examples), redacted audit-log excerpts demonstrating block events, and screenshots of our per-route tracing in the Console.
5) A mutual action plan (Excel) that maps sections of the RFP to Redwood artifacts and review owners.

Attachments I will include in the packet: redwood-egress-topology.svg, egress-evidence-2028.pdf, mutual-action-plan-novabank.xlsx.

- Do you need sample Pcap / full netflow records or are sanitized audit logs sufficient?

If you confirm, we’ll finalize and upload the packet to the Drive link and share a DocuSign-ready evidence cover.

Teresa / team — adding a couple of technical footnotes we will include in the packet for the Dedicated-with-VPC-peering scenario:

- Egress enforcement points:
  * Tenant sidecar (per-pod/process) that enforces per-tenant outbound allowlists via process-level socket policy; sidecar logs to audit stream.
  * Hypervisor/host network ACLs and per-subnet route tables — default-deny with explicit NAT endpoints for approved third-party integrations.
  * Optional egress proxy appliance in customer VPC (customer-managed) that Redwood can route through for additional inspection.

- KV/Cache segmentation: per-tenant keys and encryption-at-rest using customer-managed KMS (supported in Dedicated).
- Connectivity proof: sample flow logs (sanitized) showing a blocked outbound attempt to an unauthorized IP and subsequent alerting via our Console.

I will attach a quick excerpt of an audit log showing a rejected outbound (redacted IPs) and a suggested ACL snippet.

Kimberly Park

Teresa — quick technical confirmation on isolation and cryptography:

- All control-plane links in Dedicated deployments are TLS1.3 mutual-authenticated; keys can be backed by customer KMS when required.
- Data-plane traffic (inference payloads) between customer VPC and Redwood fabric traverses the peering link inside encrypted tunnels; we do not accept arbitrary public egress for inference payloads.
- For lateral-movement mitigation: process-level sandboxing, strict user namespaces, and per-tenant service accounts limit cross-tenant access; we will document our defense-in-depth checks and provide an example threat-lattice mapping for the packet.

I will include the sample TLS/MTLS handshake summary and a redacted KMS policy snippet in the evidence PDF.

Rishi Malhotra
Security Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
